situation.initiating: a sequence is under way and the actor has decided not to finish it — not because they misunderstood the agent, which would be repair, and not because the goal is met, which would be closing; the sequence is unwanted or going wrong, and what's needed is a way out that isn't a failure

resulting.clause: the sequence is halted where it stood, the actor has been told what if anything changed, and the exchange is back at a point where they can start something else or leave
whatever the sequence collected is now a loose end — a part-filled draft, a half-applied change — and the actor has to be able to see it to decide whether it stays
changes applied before the halt stay applied; abort states them and does not reverse them, so each one still needs a way back

situation.initiating: … [identity at the point of need](/patterns/identity-at-the-point-of-need) has led the actor to something only a full account provides—a hosted workspace, a purchase or subscription, or an organisation's access control—or they arrive at the door of a closed space or return to an account they already hold. The access step sits on a [form](/patterns/form), where the actor is either registering a new account or signing back in.
situation.resulting: Build the credential step from one or more of three parts: [passwordless access](/patterns/passwordless-access) through a code or link sent to a channel the actor controls, [federated identity](/patterns/federated-identity) through a provider they already trust, or a [password](/patterns/password) they create and store—leading with the first two where most actors hold a dependable inbox or provider account, and keeping a password for those who do not. Check the identifier and other fields with [validation](/patterns/validation), and keep [account recovery](/patterns/account-recovery) in reach from the sign-in step for when credentials fail or are forgotten. Once access is granted, lead a newcomer into [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding), or return an existing actor to their workspace…

situation.initiating: … [account access](/patterns/account-access) relies on a [password](/patterns/password) or another device-bound credential, and a returning actor cannot provide it because the secret is forgotten, lost, or compromised.
situation.resulting: Check requirements on the replacement secret as the actor types with [validation](/patterns/validation) before restoring access. When every automated route fails—because the actor has lost the email address or phone the flow relies on—hand the request off through [reaching a person](/patterns/reaching-a-person) who can restore access rather than ending in an error…

situation.initiating: … in [collaboration](/patterns/collaboration), [delegation](/patterns/delegation), and [assistance](/patterns/assistance), updates arrive from many sources across the actor's work. [Notification](/patterns/notification) carries the few events urgent enough to interrupt, while the rest wait in the places where they happened for the glance stage of [attention and tempo](/sequences/attention-and-tempo#glance).
situation.resulting: When volume grows, give the actor [filtering](/patterns/filtering) by source or event type so noisy streams do not crowd out consequential ones, and pair the stream with a clear [empty state](/patterns/state-empty) when nothing new has arrived. Where items invite discussion, attach a [conversation](/patterns/conversation) thread to the item so replies stay anchored rather than spilling into the top-level stream…

situation.initiating: things happened across actors and time that somebody now has to reconstruct — who did what, when, in what order — and the current state of the system shows the outcome with none of the path to it

resulting.clause: the path is recoverable: discrete events read as a reviewable history, each with an actor, an action, an object and a time attached
the record is what accountability now rests on, which makes what it leaves out as consequential as what it holds
histories only grow, so the log is useful in proportion to how narrowable it is — a complete record nobody can read is the same as no record

corrections and overrides that recur show in the record as a run that no single case reveals, and that run is the evidence later changes are made on: a default changed, a standing instruction written, a rule tuned, a limit widened or narrowed

situation.initiating: … the artifact is an [information environment](/patterns/information-environment) whose actors already state some of what they want in words—through search, help, a command menu, or an [outside agent](/patterns/outside-agent) reading and acting on the work. The artifact holds many objects and actions across these routes, and actors want to reach them in combinations no fixed set of controls covers.
situation.resulting: Give the actor a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) wherever they may state a request, and a [conversation](/patterns/conversation) where the exchange spans several turns; wire [searching](/patterns/searching), [help](/patterns/help) and the [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) into the same shared description of objects and actions. Where one of those fixed-vocabulary routes has nothing for what the actor typed, add an [agent fallback](/patterns/agent-fallback) to pass the unfinished request on with what was already said. Feed what the actor has open, in view or selected into each request through [view as context](/patterns/view-as-context) so words like "this" or "make it shorter" resolve without naming the target. Where a request leaves open what it refers to or what it should do, surface the interpretation with [showing the reading](/patterns/showing-the-reading) before acting, and where too much is missing for a single reading, hand off to [agent inquiry](/patterns/inquiry-agent). Weigh every act—whether triggered by a control or assembled from words—through [action consequences](/patterns/action-consequences) to set its protection, and state what lies outside the description through [capability and scope](/patterns/capability-and-scope). As actors' own names and recurring phrasing accumulate in use, feed them back into the artifact's structure through [incremental formalisation](/patterns/incremental-formalisation)…

situation.initiating: … the artifact is [addressable in words](/patterns/addressable-in-words) and the actor is working in a fixed-vocabulary control—a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu), [filtering](/patterns/filtering) or [help](/patterns/help)—when what they want has to be worked out rather than found as an existing item through [searching](/patterns/searching).
situation.resulting: Place the fallback offer inside the control's [empty state](/patterns/state-empty) and carry what the actor typed into a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) they can edit before sending to an [agent](/patterns/agent). Pass where the actor is working through [view as context](/patterns/view-as-context) so nothing has to be restated. Where the agent returns its answer as a state of the control, expose how the words were taken through [showing the reading](/patterns/showing-the-reading) so the actor can adjust one part directly; where the agent cannot fulfil the request either, state the boundary and where to go instead through [capability and scope](/patterns/capability-and-scope)…

situation.initiating: no exchange is under way and the agent has a reason to start one — work to propose, a change to report — so footing has to be established before any activity can begin: who is speaking, what it can do, and what this is about

resulting.clause: footing is set and a topic is on the table; the encounter is at its first fork, and a topic the actor accepts on any scale beyond a single question opens into an open request
the actor has been addressed but has committed to nothing; if they turn down the proposed topic and offer nothing in its place, the encounter needs an exit before it reaches any activity

situation.initiating: an activity is under way and the agent's own understanding has broken — ambiguity, low confidence, several candidate entities, a required value absent — so acting on the current reading risks doing the wrong thing confidently

resulting.clause: the agent's reading of the request is on the surface where the actor can correct it; where the trouble turns out to be one specific missing value rather than a wrong interpretation, the exchange narrows to asking for it

understanding is restored with the activity mid-flight, so completion has to be designed to resume at the step that broke rather than from the beginning — and still end in the receipt that closes the sequence

situation.initiating: the actor can state a goal but not a procedure — the steps aren't known in advance, or there are too many of them to walk through by hand — and the system holds capabilities they would otherwise have to assemble themselves

resulting.clause: there is a standing intermediary between intent and capability: the actor says what they want and something else decides how, which is both the whole benefit and the whole exposure

how much freedom the agent has to act unprompted is a setting rather than a fixed property, so the actor's trust has to be calibrated to whatever it currently is — and they have to be able to find that out
the work happened somewhere the actor wasn't watching, so it owes an account of itself afterwards to be reviewable at all
inline generation makes accepting cheaper than evaluating, so over-reliance accrues by default — deliberate friction is the countermove

situation.initiating: the content is fixed and not the actor's to change — someone else's document, a published record, a source that has to stay as it is — but their reading of it needs somewhere to live; without a layer over the top, interpretation either alters the original or stays in the actor's head

resulting.clause: the actor's interpretation sits over the content without touching it, and the marks accumulate as wear — traces of where attention and effort actually went, readable long after

once the marks are visible to others the layer stops being a private reading aid: other people read the actor's attention, and a mark becomes something that can be answered rather than only added to; few private marks are ever shared, and sharing one means rewriting it and its anchor for other readers
the layer competes with what it annotates; past some density the marks are what the reader sees, and pruning them is nobody's job by default

situation.initiating: the system is about to commit something consequential that it, not the actor, initiated — an edit, a purchase, a message sent in the actor's name — and once committed it is hard to call back

resulting.clause: nothing consequential happens without a human yes, which buys safety at the price of throughput: the agent now works at the speed of the actor's attention
each gate is an interruption, and past some frequency approving stops being a judgement and becomes the habit the gate was meant to prevent
the approval concentrates accountability: whoever clicked yes now owns an outcome they may have reviewed only glancingly

situation.initiating: pre-population has run out: the values that could be guessed from context or pulled from what the system already stores are in place, and what's left is work the actor would otherwise do themselves — which the system could take part of, if it were allowed to offer

resulting.clause: the loop is the system offering and the actor deciding, so dismissal has to stay cheap: an offer that cannot be waved away quickly is no longer an offer
each surface offers help at some level, usually chosen for typical use; some systems move the level up or down as accepted and dismissed offers accumulate
the more of the work the system takes on, the more trust the actor has to extend before accepting anything — so how an offer accounts for itself stops being decoration

the four sit at opposite ends of one spectrum and can't be tuned together: the offers a skilled actor barely notices and the offers that demand a deliberate judgement are the same move at incomparable stakes

situation.initiating: a compressed rendering — rows, cards, pins — carries a fixed subset of each entity's attributes, chosen once for everyone; the comparison the actor came to make is in the data, visible in the detail view, but absent from the view where comparing happens

resulting.clause: each view's attribute set is the actor's decision
the curation moves to the actor — surfaced sets drift and diverge, so the designed defaults still matter, now as a starting point rather than a ceiling
surfaced attributes become operable, changing what a view shows changes what the actor can do with it

situation.initiating: … people, delegated agents, and automated rules contribute to the same work under [collaboration](/patterns/collaboration), while an [activity log](/patterns/activity-log) keeps the history of what changed and [presence](/patterns/presence) shows who is active in the space right now. An [outside agent](/patterns/outside-agent) may also act in the workspace under a grant. Attribution helps complete these larger patterns by keeping contributor identity legible after the moment passes.
situation.resulting: Carry contributor identities into [commenting](/patterns/commenting) so colleagues know whom to answer, into [version history](/patterns/version-history) so actors can trace who changed what, and into [change review](/patterns/change-review) so reviewers can weigh proposed edits by author. Where a contribution was generated or revised by a model and actors need to calibrate reliance on it—or where content will be copied or exported out of the workspace—pair contributor attribution with [provenance marking](/patterns/provenance-marking) so machine involvement travels with the content itself…

situation.initiating: … in [assistance escalation](/sequences/assistance-escalation) or inside a [form](/patterns/form) field, a static guess from [good defaults](/patterns/good-defaults) has given way to the actor typing their own value, or a field draws from a set too large to show in full. This forms the reactive tier of [assisted task completion](/patterns/assisted-task-completion).
situation.resulting: When the field requires a value from a fixed set too large to display up front, pair autocomplete with [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) to turn the list into a searchable picker. Where the system already holds the actor's value in a profile, earlier session, or browser record, let [autofill](/patterns/autofill) supply it before typing begins. Pair the same narrowing list with [searching](/patterns/searching) in a query box, with [filtering](/patterns/filtering) inside a filter clause, and with a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) to locate actions and navigation targets. Where candidates shift from matching a known index to proposing related or inferred options, treat them as a [suggestion](/patterns/suggestion); and where the continuation must be generated rather than looked up, hand over to [AI completion](/patterns/ai-completion)…

situation.initiating: … in [assistance escalation](/sequences/assistance-escalation) or inside a [form](/patterns/form), a static guess from [good defaults](/patterns/good-defaults) cannot supply the actor's own specific value, yet the browser, a password manager, or the application already holds it. This forms the stored-value step near the floor of [assisted task completion](/patterns/assisted-task-completion).
situation.resulting: Pair autofill with [review before submitting](/patterns/review-before-submitting) whenever a stale or misapplied record submitted unread would carry a real cost. Where the actor is typing a value that is not stored in full—such as a lookup from a large index—use [autocomplete](/patterns/autocomplete) to complete it in flight. Where the system is proposing an inferred option for the actor to weigh rather than filling a stored record, offer a [suggestion](/patterns/suggestion) instead…

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes), the actor alters the artifact through [editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place) or a [form](/patterns/form), and those changes exist only in the running program until the system writes them to storage. This step keeps open-ended work safe without making storage an act the actor has to manage.
situation.resulting: Use this pattern as it is for open-ended work: report what was stored and when through [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback), and rely on [undo](/patterns/undo) and [version history](/patterns/version-history) to carry the recovery and milestone acts that left the Save button. Where other people can read the work while it is still changing, separate readiness from storage with [draft and publish](/patterns/draft-and-publish) so publishing becomes a deliberate act of its own. Where a real technical constraint or transaction boundary requires edits to land or be discarded as a unit, modify this arrangement with [pending changes](/patterns/pending-changes)…

situation.initiating: the content is neither prose nor a record but both by turns — parts of it want structure and parts want to stay loose, and the actor doesn't know at the outset which parts are which; a schema would demand that decision up front, and a plain writing surface would refuse to hold it at all

resulting.clause: each block carries only as much structure as currently serves it, gained or shed in place, so formalising is local and reversible instead of a commitment made before the work starts

the block is now the unit of everything the surface does — selecting, referencing, moving, commenting — so anything that addresses content addresses blocks, whether or not that matches how the actor thinks of what they wrote
every position in the document is a place where anything could go next, which puts the weight on saying *what* without having to say where

situation.initiating: … [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking) gives items and views stable addresses that restore them, and [recents](/patterns/recents) already cover short-term returns. Here the actor has reached an item, view, conversation, or position they expect to need again well after later activity has pushed it out of recents.
situation.resulting: Surface the saved list one step from navigation starting points such as a sidebar, start page, or [command menu](/patterns/command-menu). Once the list grows past what can be scanned at a glance, add [tags](/patterns/tag) or folders so the actor can organise it without planning a structure up front. Where a saved item or collection should travel to others as a curated list, pair it with [sharing](/patterns/sharing). Where the actor needs to save a filtered and sorted query rather than a single item, offer a [saved view](/patterns/data-view#saved-views)…

situation.initiating: … under [delegation](/patterns/delegation), the actor is handing work to an [agent](/patterns/agent) or an [outside agent](/patterns/outside-agent), and [permissions](/patterns/permissions) have established what it can reach. The maker now needs to let the actor settle which actions the agent may take on its own within that reach.
situation.resulting: Route pauses at a reserved action or exhausted allowance into an [approval gate](/patterns/approval-gate) to authorise the step or extend the limit, or transfer control through a [handoff](/patterns/handoff) with a summary of what was used and what remains. Rate which categories of act may run freely and which need a checkpoint using [action consequences](/patterns/action-consequences), pair spend and quota caps with [cost transparency](/patterns/cost-transparency), and warn before a ceiling is hit through [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback). Where boundaries combine several conditions, let the actor edit them through [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition), and offer a [trial run](/patterns/trial-run) over sample cases before live work begins. Keep standing grants inspectable and revocable in [settings](/patterns/settings) between runs, and record every autonomous action, refusal, and limit reached in the [activity log](/patterns/activity-log) so the actor can widen or narrow the grant from evidence…

situation.initiating: a value the actor must supply from a set they didn't author and may not be able to survey

resulting.clause: a visible, narrowable candidate set that converges on a valid committed value

situation.initiating: … the actor is working in a [session](/patterns/session), a [conversation](/patterns/conversation), or a [version history](/patterns/version-history) where [undo](/patterns/undo) only moves along one sequence. Here they are at an earlier turn or checkpoint and want to take more than one direction from it.
situation.resulting: Where the actor needs to weigh what diverged across sibling branches, align their outputs or paths with [comparing](/patterns/comparing). Where a tree overview sits beside the active transcript, link them as [coordinated views](/patterns/coordinated-views) so selecting a node scopes the view. Where the change only retries a single turn at the leaf, use [regeneration](/patterns/regeneration) or [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) rather than adding a long-lived branch. When a branch settles on a result that should replace or join the main line, bring it back through [change review](/patterns/change-review) or [reconciliation](/patterns/reconciliation); when only a finished piece needs to carry forward, lift it out with [extraction](/patterns/extraction)…

situation.initiating: the actor is about to ask for something and has no reliable read on what this agent can do; a conversational surface looks identical whether it can act, only retrieve, or only talk, so the boundary has to be stated rather than discovered by walking into it

resulting.clause: the actor knows what is in and out of scope before spending a turn on it, and an out-of-scope request meets a refusal with somewhere to go rather than a dead end
the statement is now a promise the rest of the exchange is held to; capability that turns out narrower than stated reads as the agent having misled them
the statement is true for this encounter only; what the agent can do changes between visits, so the boundary is stated again on return wherever it has changed

situation.initiating: … a standing rule, filter, recommender, or agent has acted on a case the actor did not want touched, or left alone one they did, and the actor is looking at that case: in the result, in a [notification](/patterns/notification), or among the items the rule refused. Even where a [trial run](/patterns/trial-run) checked the rule beforehand, cases arrive in use that the trial did not meet. Where the fault is in the wording or shape of a generated draft rather than in a standing decision on a case, the repair is an [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) of that output.
situation.resulting: Support the smallest repair with [undo](/patterns/undo) or a one-off skip that leaves the standing behaviour untouched. Attach an [explanation](/patterns/explanation) to the case showing which rule, signal, or preference produced it, so a deeper change can start from the matching reason. When an override should hold beyond this item or the same correction recurs across cases, lead from the case into [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition) on the matching clauses or into a [standing instruction](/patterns/standing-instructions) in the actor's own words. Where the actor can show the right handling on the case more easily than state a rule for it, hand over to [tuning by demonstration](/patterns/tuning-by-demonstration). Keep the list of standing exceptions open to review so accumulated overrides do not silently cancel the rule they qualify…

situation.initiating: … someone else—a colleague returning a separate copy under [draft and publish](/patterns/draft-and-publish) in [working on the same thing](/sequences/working-on-the-same-thing), or an agent returning [generated content](/patterns/generated-content) in [delegating a task](/sequences/delegating-a-task) or a [trial run](/patterns/trial-run)—has proposed changes to existing work the actor is responsible for. The proposed changes have arrived and are waiting for the actor's decision before taking effect.
situation.resulting: Draw the diff with [comparing](/patterns/comparing)'s version case, assuming the shared structure and showing only what changed. Where the system proposed the change and applying it carries consequences, place an [approval gate](/patterns/approval-gate) on the review so approval binds to the specific change. Pair the review with [commenting](/patterns/commenting) so discussion attaches to individual changes rather than the whole document, and use [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) to record the review outcome when colleagues review each other's work. Keep [undo](/patterns/undo) available after changes are accepted and applied, not only as rejection beforehand. Where the system made the change and there is no author to ask, attach a [work trail](/patterns/work-trail) alongside the diff so the actor can check how it was produced, keeping in mind that the model's narration can be wrong…

situation.initiating: … [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) spans more than one sitting, and several of the setup and learning tasks that bring the actor to competent use can be taken in any order. Charted progress gives that onboarding a bounded path the actor can return to across sessions.
situation.resulting: Report each completed milestone through [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) at the moment it finishes, and update the list so the actor always sees where they stand. Where a single milestone involves an ordered sequence of inputs of its own, let [step by step](/patterns/step-by-step) carry the actor through that item before returning them to the list. Where the right next move depends on the actor's specific data or behaviour rather than a shared set of milestones, hand off to [next-best action](/patterns/next-best-action) instead of a fixed checklist…

situation.initiating: … the system has produced [generated content](/patterns/generated-content) whose claims the actor did not write: an answer in a conversation, a report built from [reference material](/patterns/reference-material), or a [text lens](/patterns/text-lens) summary compressing a longer document. Citation helps complete these larger patterns when the actor needs to verify claims against their sources.
situation.resulting: Give each marker a [link preview](/patterns/link-preview) of the cited span so the actor can weigh the passage in place before opening the full source. Where a claim has no source passage behind it, or its sources disagree, mark the span with [expressed uncertainty](/patterns/expressed-uncertainty) graded by that evidence rather than attaching a weak link or leaving the gap silent. Place citations ahead of any [explanation](/patterns/explanation) so the actor meets the sources before a rationale that makes checking less likely. Where the answer took several steps to produce, pair citations with a [work trail](/patterns/work-trail) so the actor can inspect the path taken alongside the passages each claim rests on. Because citation marks raise trust on sight even when nobody follows them, add [cognitive forcing functions](/patterns/cognitive-forcing-functions) at acceptance where the stakes require the actor to verify before committing…

situation.initiating: the goal that brought the actor here is met, or they have signalled they're done — the activity is finished but the encounter is still open, and cutting it off here forfeits whatever they hadn't got around to raising

resulting.clause: the encounter is ended deliberately: last topics were invited and either handled or scheduled, and both parties know it's over rather than parked
anything raised in the close and deferred is now an outstanding commitment the actor is expecting to be kept, outside this exchange

situation.initiating: a system recommendation is on the surface and accepting it costs less than evaluating it; the actor has the competence to judge and the stakes to warrant judging, but nothing in the interaction asks them to, so deferral accrues by default — and explanation alone won't fix it, since a plausible rationale can make rubber-stamping easier rather than harder

resulting.clause: the actor has had to do something — wait, commit an answer first, name a reason, finish an incomplete argument — before accepting, so the judgement on record is theirs; where that something was writing down why, the reasons accumulate into a trail somebody else can read
the friction is real and paid on every decision, so it holds only where the stakes keep justifying it; where they don't, actors learn the shortest path through it
the help lands unevenly — it works best on actors already inclined to think, and least on the ones most likely to defer, who are the reason for it

situation.initiating: several actors are working toward one outcome and each can only see their own part; with no shared account of what is happening they duplicate work, overwrite each other, and lose track of who owes what to whom

resulting.clause: work that was independent becomes joint: participants can see what others did, follow the reasoning behind it, and converge without needing to meet
agency is distributed and renegotiated turn by turn rather than held by anyone, so who decides is a live question at every step rather than a settled one
coordination now runs in a rhythm — synchronous or asynchronous — and that rhythm decides what kinds of disagreement can be resolved at all

situation.initiating: … in [learning](/sequences/learning) and [structuring the space](/sequences/structuring-the-space), the artifact has accumulated more operations and destinations than persistent toolbars and menus can carry, and is being made [addressable in words](/patterns/addressable-in-words) — or, at the caret, shaped as a [block-based editor](/patterns/block-based-editor). This pattern specialises [searching](/patterns/searching) over the artifact's commands and destinations rather than its content. Where the actor has already selected a target on screen and only needs a routine operation on it, [contextual actions](/patterns/contextual-actions) already serve that moment.
situation.resulting: Before the actor types a character, open the command menu onto [recents](/patterns/recents) and saved [bookmarks](/patterns/bookmarking) so returning to a recent action or a pinned destination takes no typing at all. As the actor types, pair the input with [autocomplete](/patterns/autocomplete) that matches fragments, initials, and synonyms across command names and parameters, since naming only helps when the actor does not need the exact label up front. Show [keyboard shortcuts](/patterns/keyboard-shortcuts) beside each entry so every lookup rehearses the direct key bindings that carry the actor toward [mastery](/patterns/mastery). Inside a text field or editor, let a trigger character such as a slash open the command menu at the caret to apply [prestructured formatting](/patterns/prestructured-formatting) without leaving the line. Filter the list to actions that apply in the current state, and handle [unavailable actions](/patterns/unavailable-actions) that the actor still expects to find by keeping them searchable with the reason they cannot run here rather than letting them vanish without trace. Where the actor describes an outcome in their own words and no command matches, offer an [agent fallback](/patterns/agent-fallback), which takes what they typed and returns the matching command with its arguments filled in. When the request combines several operations or asks for new content that no single command in the vocabulary covers, hand the input off to a [prompt](/patterns/prompt)…

situation.initiating: … [sharing](/patterns/sharing) or a [change review](/patterns/change-review) has brought several people onto the same document, design, or change inside a wider [collaboration](/patterns/collaboration). Unlike private [annotation](/patterns/annotation), which marks a passage for the person who made the mark, the remarks here are directed at other collaborators.
situation.resulting: Show where each thread stands—open, answered, or resolved—with [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) so the comment layer does not only grow. Alert participants to replies through [notifications](/patterns/notification), and record who said what over time in the [activity log](/patterns/activity-log). Where people begin referring to a commented passage rather than only discussing it, let [incremental formalisation](/patterns/incremental-formalisation) promote it into an addressable quote while keeping its place in the text and its thread…

situation.initiating: … the actor has two or more items designated by [selection](/patterns/selection) or by the system—versions of one item in [change review](/patterns/change-review), [reconciliation](/patterns/reconciliation), or [version history](/patterns/version-history), or instances and subsets while [making sense at scale](/sequences/making-sense-at-scale). Here they need to see what differs between them.
situation.resulting: Where one version is a proposed change to existing work, build [change review](/patterns/change-review) on the version case and add part-by-part acceptance. Where the versions are two actors' divergent work on the same item, build [reconciliation](/patterns/reconciliation) on it so a person picks between them. Use the same version case in [version history](/patterns/version-history) to show a past state beside the current one before restoring it. Keep [selection](/patterns/selection) lightweight so the actor can pick or swap which items enter the comparison…

situation.initiating: … inside a [data view](/patterns/data-view), a [block-based editor](/patterns/block-based-editor), or a canvas, the actor has designated a target through a [selection](/patterns/selection) or by pointing at an element—a text span, a document block, an object, or rows in a list—and is about to act on it directly rather than searching for an operation by name in a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu).
situation.resulting: On selected text or blocks, host [prestructured formatting](/patterns/prestructured-formatting), [commenting](/patterns/commenting), and [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) directly on the floating toolbar; on selected items or rows, host [tag](/patterns/tag) assignment, [deletion](/patterns/deletion), and, when two or more items are selected, [comparing](/patterns/comparing). Omit controls that do not apply rather than showing them disabled, following [unavailable actions](/patterns/unavailable-actions), and display [keyboard shortcuts](/patterns/keyboard-shortcuts) beside menu items so actors can bypass the menu on repeat use. Where the actor states a request in words against the same selection rather than picking a preset action, bind the target through [view as context](/patterns/view-as-context)…

situation.initiating: an evolving exchange between actors where meaning has to be built up over multiple turns rather than stated in one

resulting.clause: a dialogue structure that carries context forward, lets either party take a turn, and accommodates repair when alignment slips

situation.initiating: several views of one model already coexist — each earning its place by showing a different aspect — but relating them is the actor's job: find the item here, re-find it there, carry the correspondence in working memory

resulting.clause: designating something in one view marks it in every view where it appears; cross-view relationships — correlations invisible in any single view — arrive perceptually instead of being reconstructed
every added view charges for what the coupling buys, in learning time, working memory, screen space, and upkeep

each coupling is now a correctness surface: a false cue implies a relationship that doesn't hold, and propagation slower than ~100 ms reads as no relationship at all — the cues, not just the data, can lie

situation.initiating: machine work costs compute, money, and time that are invisible at the point of asking; unseen, the cost surfaces later as an exhausted quota, a bill, or work quietly throttled

resulting.clause: the cost of asking is visible before and during the work — estimates up front, meters while it runs, quotas in view — so spending becomes a decision instead of a discovery
visible meters change behaviour: actors ration exploration, and the counter's presence taxes exactly the open-ended use the system is best at
cost talk imports the provider's economics into the interaction; the unit shown (tokens, credits, currency) frames what the actor thinks they are buying

situation.initiating: … the artifact is an [information environment](/patterns/information-environment) that the actor reaches through more than one channel: a website and a phone app, an email or a notification that points into it, an agent that answers questions about it. The channels were often made by different teams or at different times, and the actor moves between them in the middle of a piece of work.
situation.resulting: Give every item an address that resolves across channels with [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking), and carry that address in every [notification](/patterns/notification) so it opens the item itself rather than the artifact's front door. Keep view arrangements with the actor's account through [remembered state](/patterns/remembered-state) so they travel across devices. Where the work lives on the actor's own device, use [sync through own storage](/patterns/sync-through-own-storage) to bring it to their other devices…

situation.initiating: a collection too large or varied to absorb whole, and an actor whose purpose fixes what matters in it right now — which items, rendered how, ordered by what

resulting.clause: the collection reaches the actor already framed — queried, represented, arranged — and the framing is inspectable and adjustable rather than baked in
a framed population of items makes designating some of them for action cheap; what the framing exposes is what selection can operate on

situation.initiating: … [structuring the space](/sequences/structuring-the-space) has produced a layout, and the actor can reach states that took several moves to assemble: a context switched to, an item opened, a list narrowed, a step in [step by step](/patterns/step-by-step), or a position and scale in a [pan and zoom](/patterns/pan-and-zoom) space. That state may need to be handed to another actor in [working on the same thing](/sequences/working-on-the-same-thing), reopened from a notice in [attention and tempo](/sequences/attention-and-tempo), or returned to after an absence in [memory and continuity](/sequences/memory-and-continuity).
situation.resulting: Because an addressable link travels beyond the actor's control, decide with [sharing](/patterns/sharing) who may open it, and give the holder a [link preview](/patterns/link-preview) of what lies at the destination, scrolled to the part the address points inside. Give each [comment](/patterns/commenting) and each message in a thread an address of its own, and let the address carry what [progressive disclosure](/patterns/progressive-disclosure) has revealed where that narrows the view. Keep every named state resolving as the space behind it is reorganised, and where a view changes in place rather than by navigation, decide which changes become a Back step…

situation.initiating: a stretch of activity in which the actor wants to remove data, with consequences that range from trivial to permanent and far-reaching

resulting.clause: a removal path matched to the severity, reversibility, and scope of the loss — confirmation, undo, soft delete, or typed challenge
the data is gone; whether that holds is now a question of recovery — a completed deletion is exactly the state undo acts on

situation.initiating: the exchange is mid-activity and one party has to step away — idle, interrupted, a dropped connection — with the goal still unmet; a formal close would misstate where things stand, and dropping it silently loses the work

resulting.clause: the exchange is parked rather than ended: a saved state whose persistence the actor can see — something either opening now has to act on, re-entering with history rather than starting fresh
parked state ages while nobody is watching it, so the assumptions inside it may not hold on return; confirming them is part of resuming, not an extra

situation.initiating: … several people, teams or organisations take part in the same work in a [workspace](/patterns/workspace), each answering for a different part of it, and an organisation that brings others in still has to answer for what happens to its own work and members.
situation.resulting: Use [sharing](/patterns/sharing) to let people across a line into a part they do not hold by default, and use [roles](/patterns/roles) to grade what each person may do once inside…

situation.initiating: storage is continuous, so the actor's work is always safe — but nothing marks the point where it is ready for others to read, and in a shared artefact that means whatever state the work is in is what everyone else sees

resulting.clause: the version others read stays put while the actor works, so unfinished work is never mistaken for the finished thing
publishing is a deliberate act, which gives review, versioning, and notification a natural point to attach to
the artefact now exists in two versions, and the actor has to manage the gap: forgetting to publish leaves readers on an outdated version
publishing reaches every reader at once, so in a shared artefact it can be a heavier act than any deletion, and it is rated for confirmation and a way back like the other acts

situation.initiating: the item to operate on and the destination that stands for the outcome are both on screen, and asking for the operation by name — a menu, a form, a command — would restate what the actor can already point at

resulting.clause: the operation happens where its object and outcome are visible, and the result reads off the surface afterwards — the item sits where it was put, and the state is its own receipt
destinations are now part of the operation's vocabulary: each must mean exactly one thing, refuse what it cannot accept, and stay legible while a drag is in flight
every dragged operation exists twice — the gesture and its drag-free twin — and the pair must perform the identical write, or the interface holds two truths

situation.initiating: the corpus has grown past what anyone linked by hand; the explicit links are the connections somebody thought to make at the time of writing, and what the actor is after are the ones nobody did

resulting.clause: latent connections are on the surface as ranked suggestions, which lets the actor follow them without the system having claimed any of them are real structure
the suggested links are unfamiliar by construction — nobody authored them, so the actor has no prior expectation of where any one leads, and link text alone no longer tells them
the corpus holds more valid connections than anyone can read, so what the actor sees is whatever survived a ranking and a cutoff — and both are invisible to them

situation.initiating: the actor is looking at the thing they want to change, and the way to change it is somewhere else — a form, a dialog, another page — so making the change means translating what they see into someone else's arrangement of it and coming back to find out whether it landed

resulting.clause: the artefact is its own control, so the change is seen in its final context as it is made, with nothing to translate between an input arrangement and a result
the display carries an editing affordance it did not need before, and that affordance competes with the same surface's job as something to read
an affordance revealed on approach reaches whoever can hover and nobody else, unless a touch and keyboard route is built alongside it

changes commit one at a time — the short gap between act and effect is what makes the result feel caused by the gesture — so there is no assembled set to review and no pending state to cancel from; taking something back happens after the fact
changing is always one gesture away, so stray input reaches the record — an exposure proportional to how much the artefact is read rather than written

situation.initiating: … the actor is working in an artifact that keeps [sessions](/patterns/session), history, recent items, and personal context by default. Here they are starting a sensitive question, a search on a shared device, an off-profile experiment, or a one-off task they do not want carried into their account record.
situation.resulting: Keep the non-saving state visible throughout with [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback), and open the session with a brief [explanation](/patterns/explanation) of what is withheld from the [activity log](/patterns/activity-log), [recents](/patterns/recents), [remembered state](/patterns/remembered-state), and [memory](/patterns/memory)—and what still leaves a record outside the artifact. Where an ephemeral exchange produces a result worth keeping, let the actor lift it out with [extraction](/patterns/extraction) without logging the surrounding thread. For normal sessions that turn out to be disposable only at the end, pair this with single-action [deletion](/patterns/deletion) so the actor does not have to decide up front…

situation.initiating: the system did something the actor didn't expect or can't act on — a rule fired, an option isn't there, a recommendation arrived — and the reason for it lives inside the system rather than on the surface; left there, the actor either guesses at it or defers to the system wholesale

resulting.clause: the reasoning is legible, so the actor can judge when to trust the system and when to override it — which is a different capability from being able to operate it

a complete and plausible explanation can make deferring *easier* rather than harder: the actor now holds a justification they didn't have to think through, which is the state a forcing function exists to interrupt

an explanation pitched at the actor's level is a guess about that level — too much depth reads as noise, too little as evasion, and the actor can't ask for the difference unless the depth is theirs to move

situation.initiating: … the system has produced [generated content](/patterns/generated-content) or offered a [suggestion](/patterns/suggestion) whose parts are not equally well supported, including claims that [citation](/patterns/citation) could not link to a source passage or whose sources disagree. Expressed uncertainty helps complete these patterns when the actor needs to tell well-supported parts from guesses.
situation.resulting: Where the stakes of accepting a doubtful span or proposal are high, pair the uncertainty mark with [cognitive forcing functions](/patterns/cognitive-forcing-functions) and exclude low-confidence items from bulk acceptance so the actor's pause lands on the uncertain parts. Where the output draws on external sources, pair the marks with [citation](/patterns/citation) so the actor can inspect the agreeing or conflicting passages directly…

situation.initiating: the actor needs content that won't fit one turn — instructions, an explanation, a narrative — and the single-turn forms have either been tried or are visibly too small for it; the agent has to hold the floor across several turns without losing them

resulting.clause: the telling runs as a structured sequence the actor controls: scope announced up front, each step advanced on their continuer, and skip, back and stop available throughout

holding the floor suppresses the actor's turn, so trouble that would have surfaced as an interruption now has to be invited — support moves at every step, and a visible way out of the telling into another activity

situation.initiating: the work has produced something that now matters more than the transaction that produced it — a document, a decision, a piece of code — and that transaction is the only place it exists: no name of its own, no address to link to, nothing to reopen, so finding it again means finding the exchange and scrolling

resulting.clause: the extracted thing has an identity of its own — nameable, linkable, reopenable — which is what a ladder of representations needs before it can render one thing at several depths
what the host keeps at the point of extraction — the whole thing, a pointer, or nothing — decides whether the exchange still reads afterwards as a record of what happened
the exchange becomes disposable and the thing does not: value moves out of the transcript, and whatever was never extracted is what gets lost when the exchange is closed
the offer has to arrive when the thing turns out to matter, which is usually after it was made and rarely when the actor is thinking about where to file it

situation.initiating: … the actor is working in the artifact, during [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) or long after it, and a capability that would serve what they are doing is one they have not met: either an existing function they never encountered, or one that has just been added or changed.
situation.resulting: Record whether the actor has seen, dismissed, or tried the prompt in [remembered state](/patterns/remembered-state), so the same tip is never shown twice and returns only if the capability itself changes. Keep [help](/patterns/help) as the pull channel the actor can consult on demand, so proactive offers and actor-initiated lookup divide the work between them. Surface faster execution routes in the same way, placing [keyboard shortcuts](/patterns/keyboard-shortcuts) as hints beside the slower controls the actor is already using. In a [layered interface](/patterns/layered-interface), use contextual discovery to show what the next layer holds when the actor's work reaches the boundary of the current one. When an important change must reach actors who are away from the surface where it lives, route the announcement through a [notification](/patterns/notification)…

situation.initiating: … [account access](/patterns/account-access) is in place for registration and sign-in, and the actor already holds a verified identity with an external provider such as Google, Apple, or an enterprise directory, rather than relying on a standalone [password](/patterns/password).
situation.resulting: Where actors need sign-in without third-party platform coupling, offer [passwordless access](/patterns/passwordless-access) instead, and where an actor holds no supported provider account, keep a [password](/patterns/password) alongside it…

situation.initiating: … a [data view](/patterns/data-view) has framed a collection, and the actor's question concerns only part of it. There are too many items to scan, and the actor can say what distinguishes the ones they want.
situation.resulting: Build each condition's value picker as a [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) over the property's known values, and pair the filtered view with [sorting](/patterns/sorting) and [grouping](/patterns/grouping) so the actor can order and arrange what the conditions let through. When no items match, keep the active conditions in view inside the [empty state](/patterns/state-empty) and show which one emptied the list. Where conditions have to be combined with and, or and not, or saved to run again later, hand off to [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition); where the actor types a criterion that no recorded property names, pass the unfinished query on through an [agent fallback](/patterns/agent-fallback)…

situation.initiating: the work has been partitioned into contexts, and this one is a workspace with a rich toolset — an editor, a console — where the tools are heterogeneous but few enough to sit on one surface, and leaving the surface to reach one would break the work

resulting.clause: everything is reachable in one place — which holds only while the tools and destinations fit one surface; when the item count outgrows the screen, hub and spoke takes over

situation.initiating: the actor is attending to one point inside something large — one event in a long record, one part of a deep structure — and needs it in full without losing the whole; a second view costs screen they don't have, and a scale control would take the surroundings away as it brought the point closer

resulting.clause: everything stays on screen, told unevenly: the focus in full, its surroundings coarser the further out they stand, and nothing moves as attention shifts

the actor steers the lens but the system decides what counts as near, so the distance metric — position along a sequence, steps through a structure, a model's confidence — is doing editorial work under the appearance of geometry
the coarse rungs are summaries something has to produce, and at the rim they may be generated; generated text then sits in a place the actor reads as structure

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes), a [form](/patterns/form), a [conversation](/patterns/conversation) turn, or an [inline interface](/patterns/inline-interface) needs a value the actor holds in a loose or variable form, where a [structured format](/patterns/structured-format) does not fit the input.
situation.resulting: Because the system or an [agent](/patterns/agent) did the structuring, report what was parsed through [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) and confirm it with [showing the reading](/patterns/showing-the-reading) before it counts as agreed. Mark doubtful readings with [expressed uncertainty](/patterns/expressed-uncertainty), and expose why a reading was chosen through [explanation](/patterns/explanation) when stakes warrant it. Follow parsing with [validation](/patterns/validation) for errors the parser cannot catch, and pair it with [localization](/patterns/localization) so regional dates, numbers, and addresses are read in the actor's locale. Where loose input populates several fields at once, end with [review before submitting](/patterns/review-before-submitting) so extracted values do not go through unread…

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes) the actor has reached the point of saying what the change is, and it takes several related answers: the fields only make sense together, need more room than the display offers, or apply to a set rather than the item in view. [Editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place) handles the single value; a form is the surface for the set. The editor for a standing instruction in [delegating a task](/sequences/delegating-a-task) uses the same surface for a set of fields that stays open.
situation.resulting: Choose a move for each field in the order of the [making changes](/sequences/making-changes) form sub-sequence: [forgiving format](/patterns/forgiving-format) or [structured format](/patterns/structured-format) for the format of the answer, [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) where the value comes from a fixed set, [good defaults](/patterns/good-defaults) pre-filled, [autocomplete](/patterns/autocomplete) and [autofill](/patterns/autofill) finishing or supplying a value, and [validation](/patterns/validation) answering an unacceptable input at the field that produced it. Where the set is large or the commitment costly, end with a [review before submitting](/patterns/review-before-submitting), and let [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) report what the submission did. Where a form outgrows one screen, split it into parts with [sections](/patterns/sections), reveal depth as it becomes relevant with [progressive disclosure](/patterns/progressive-disclosure), or move to one question per page with [step by step](/patterns/step-by-step); where later questions depend on earlier answers, turn it into a [wizard](/patterns/wizard). Hold the fields as [pending changes](/patterns/pending-changes) until submitted—or pair with [automatic saving](/patterns/automatic-saving) to keep a half-filled form safe—and let [localization](/patterns/localization) govern which formats its fields accept…

situation.initiating: the work has been partitioned into contexts, and this one holds a small set of heterogeneous sections between which the actor moves routinely — few enough that a menu can name them all on every page, and cross-section journeys common enough that a return through a hub would be paid on every trip

resulting.clause: every destination is one move from every other, and the shape of the whole is visible from anywhere — bought with screen space on every page, spent whether or not the actor on that page needs it

the global menu is a fixed budget that content growth eats into; the set that has to fit the chrome stops fitting long before the content stops arriving, and what gives is either the depth on show or the topology

situation.initiating: … the artifact has an [agent](/patterns/agent) in it, and part of what the actor reads and works on was produced by it from a [prompt](/patterns/prompt), [reference material](/patterns/reference-material), and the context it was given, including what [memory](/patterns/memory) carried in. The output may be a reply in a [conversation](/patterns/conversation), a draft, a set of edits, or a generated interface.
situation.resulting: Let the actor steer the output in words with [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision), which works from the output they have, or request another version through [regeneration](/patterns/regeneration), which draws again from the request, for the whole output or for a selected passage. Where the request itself was at fault, let them change the [prompt](/patterns/prompt) and draw again from it, and where they already have the wording in mind, [editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place) is more direct. Move corrections that have to be repeated on every run into [standing instructions](/patterns/standing-instructions). Ground individual claims in their sources with [citation](/patterns/citation), mark weakly supported parts with [expressed uncertainty](/patterns/expressed-uncertainty), and label machine output with [provenance marking](/patterns/provenance-marking) when it mixes with human writing or leaves the tool. Pair the result with a [work trail](/patterns/work-trail) or [explanation](/patterns/explanation) to show how it was produced, and add [cognitive forcing functions](/patterns/cognitive-forcing-functions) before acceptance where an unchecked error would be costly. When the actor is ready to commit the output, use [change review](/patterns/change-review) to accept edits to existing content piece by piece, [extraction](/patterns/extraction) to save a result as a standalone item, or [next-best action](/patterns/next-best-action) to propose the next step…

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes) or at the start of [assistance escalation](/sequences/assistance-escalation), a [form](/patterns/form) or a [wizard](/patterns/wizard) step now holds fields and [bounded choices](/patterns/bounded-choice), and [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) has routine setup decisions to settle before the actor reaches their first result. Where typical use, general context, or [remembered state](/patterns/remembered-state) already points to a safe value, those fields do not need to start blank for [forgiving](/patterns/forgiving-format) or [structured format](/patterns/structured-format) entry.
situation.resulting: Pair defaults with [localization](/patterns/localization) so locale-dependent guesses such as language, timezone, and formats match the actor's region. Where the actor starts typing a value of their own, hand over to [autocomplete](/patterns/autocomplete) for completion in flight; where the system already holds the actor's actual value in a profile, earlier session, or browser record, let [autofill](/patterns/autofill) take over from guessing. Where a static guess stops sufficing and the system needs to participate in the work itself, continue into [assisted task completion](/patterns/assisted-task-completion). Where a standing default does not fit an actor on an axis they care about, let them override it once in [settings](/patterns/settings) so the preference holds across sessions; and where confidence is too low to pre-fill a value directly, offer a [suggestion](/patterns/suggestion) instead of committing a guess on the actor's behalf…

situation.initiating: the collection is flat and the actor's question is about subsets rather than items — which cluster is largest, which is behind, how two of them compare — and a flat list gives them nothing to compare

resulting.clause: the collection has visible structure along a chosen attribute, so differences between subsets are readable without the actor tallying anything by hand
the grouping attribute is a claim about which of an item's attributes matters most, and an item that genuinely belongs in two groups has to be filed in one
headers cost space and carry collapse state, so a grouping that yields many small groups fragments the list it was meant to organise

situation.initiating: … work is under way—assigned to an [agent](/patterns/agent) in [governing autonomy](/sequences/governing-autonomy) or [delegating standing work](/sequences/delegating-standing-work), or carried by a participant in [working on the same thing](/sequences/working-on-the-same-thing)—and whoever holds it cannot continue alone because a limit in [bounded autonomy](/patterns/bounded-autonomy) was reached, human credentials or a colleague's review are needed, or the actor stepped in to take over. The work is still live rather than halted with [abort](/patterns/abort), and the obstacle calls for a change of holder rather than an in-place fix through [agent repair](/patterns/agent-repair).
situation.resulting: Close the transfer through explicit acceptance or refusal in [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback), bind a [deep link](/patterns/deep-linking) directly to the stopped item and state, and alert an absent receiver with a [notification](/patterns/notification). Where the transfer must locate an owner, admin, or specialist outside the current run, open the route through [reaching a person](/patterns/reaching-a-person). Keep the underlying trace inspectable in the [activity log](/patterns/activity-log) and sign every handoff, acceptance, and return with [attribution](/patterns/attribution) so the record shows who held the work at each point. Once the actor takes over directly, give them [editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place) on the live artifact, and where they must remain able to perform the task themselves, support [mastery](/patterns/mastery) alongside delegated runs. Where the agent only needed a single action authorised or a limit raised to carry on, use an [approval gate](/patterns/approval-gate) instead of transferring the rest of the task…

situation.initiating: … within the artifact's [information environment](/patterns/information-environment), during [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) or long after it, the actor encounters a task, term, or behaviour they cannot work out from the surface alone. Unlike [feature discovery](/patterns/feature-discovery), where the artifact offers capabilities nobody asked about, help serves an actor who brings a question.
situation.resulting: Attach brief in-place answers to the controls that raise questions using [annotation](/patterns/annotation), and give the reason behind a specific event—such as a disabled option or a rule that fired—as an [explanation](/patterns/explanation) at that point. Pair failure recovery in [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) with help that says what to do next. Index help pages for [searching](/patterns/searching) and the [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) under the words actors use as well as the artifact's own labels, and keep external documentation aligned with the interface through [cross-channel continuity](/patterns/cross-channel-continuity) so each links to the other under the same names. Where a page must serve readers at different levels of familiarity or detail, add a [text lens](/patterns/text-lens); author separate versions where content differs by plan, role, platform, or release. In an artifact [addressable in words](/patterns/addressable-in-words), resolve help queries against the same description of objects and actions that the command menu and agents read. Where written pages do not cover the actor's case, use [agent fallback](/patterns/agent-fallback) to pass the question to an [agent](/patterns/agent) grounded in the help pages with [citations](/patterns/citation), and where the fix requires access, authority, or judgement someone else holds, route the actor to [reaching a person](/patterns/reaching-a-person)…

situation.initiating: … the work has been divided into contexts in [structuring the space](/sequences/structuring-the-space), and one context holds sections that differ in kind and are used one at a time—or a [flat surface](/patterns/flat-navigation) has outgrown the screen. Switching across a set of [workspaces](/patterns/workspace) presents the same structure.
situation.resulting: Design what the hub reports across the spokes as a [purpose-keyed view](/patterns/purpose-keyed-view) in its own right, built for the actor's recurring question rather than inherited from the topology; [making sense at scale](/sequences/making-sense-at-scale) takes that up. Give actors who know their destination a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) and [searching](/patterns/searching) to reach a spoke without the hub, and use [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking) so spokes can be reached from outside the structure altogether. When cross-spoke traffic becomes general, switch to [fully connected](/patterns/fully-connected) (such as a persistent tab bar on a phone) rather than patching the hub, or use a [hybrid](/patterns/hybrid-patterns) that keeps the hub for most sections while directly linking the few routine pairs. Where the sections nest rather than sit beside each other, hold the depth in a [multilevel tree](/patterns/multilevel-tree)…

situation.initiating: the actor's own competence is the thing the system was meant to support, and always seeing the recommendation first is quietly eroding it; the other forcing functions interrupt a single decision, and what's at stake here is the skill across all of them — which only survives if it is occasionally used unaided

resulting.clause: the actor has an unaided answer on record before they see the system's, so the comparison teaches whichever way the mismatch runs — including the way that confirms they were right
the value sits in the comparison, not the withholding: a bare "you said X, the system said Y" charges the actor for unaided work and returns nothing for it
withholding is expensive enough that it can only run some of the time, which makes how often a live decision rather than a settled one — and one the actor has a stake in

nodes.title: Identity at the point of need

situation.initiating: … the artifact is divided into [workspaces](/patterns/workspace), and its features reach points where an identity could be asked for: when the actor arrives, keeps their work, opens it on another device, lets another person in, or pays. Whether the work lives on the provider's server or on the actor's own device, under [local-first ownership](/patterns/local-first-ownership), decides which of those points need an identity at all.
situation.resulting: On a hosted artifact, let the actor start without an identity through [immediate use](/patterns/immediate-use); where they only need to return to the same work on the same device, cover it with [resuming](/patterns/resuming) instead. When a need reaches beyond the device, meet it with the lightest move that fits: use [sync through own storage](/patterns/sync-through-own-storage) to keep work across devices or backed up off the device, [sharing](/patterns/sharing) to let another person in—with a link carrying access when the recipient does not need an account—and [account access](/patterns/account-access) only when a hosted workspace, paid entitlement, or organisation access control requires a full account…

situation.initiating: … under [identity at the point of need](/patterns/identity-at-the-point-of-need), an artifact asks for an identity only when a task genuinely requires one. An actor arrives at the artifact to explore its tools, evaluate its fit, or complete a discrete task, before any need for an account has arisen. This pattern gives the artifact its entrance at that opening threshold, where no identity has yet been declared.
situation.resulting: Keep draft state in browser storage or encode it in [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking), and pair with [resuming](/patterns/resuming) so in-flight work survives across visits and reloads. Where the artifact offers starter templates or exploratory tasks, lead directly into [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) so the first result arrives before any request for an account…

situation.initiating: … work moves between the artifact and the other [tools its actors use](/patterns/tool-ecology), and a [reference](/patterns/reference-material) will not do: the other tool cannot follow a link, the work has to arrive in a form the other tool can change, or the actor is gathering in what they made elsewhere. The copy that results is separate from its source from the moment it is made.
situation.resulting: Mark every exported copy with [provenance marking](/patterns/provenance-marking) of where and when it came from so a later reader can tell which of two diverging versions is the source. Design export formats alongside [local-first ownership](/patterns/local-first-ownership) so the actor can always take their work to another program. Where the other tool can follow a link and does not need its own editable copy, use [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking) instead to keep a single source…

situation.initiating: content entered informally has grown regularities — a label applied again and again, near-synonyms circling one meaning, prose that behaves like a list, a field everyone fills the same way — or a single informal piece has started to be relied on beyond the note it was written as; demanding the schema up front was rightly refused: the vocabulary was still moving, and structure asked for early is structure guessed

resulting.clause: structure arrives after evidence rather than before it, so the schema records what the content turned out to be instead of what someone predicted it would be
every promotion is chosen or offered, never imposed, and stays reversible — a declined offer costs nothing, and a promoted structure can be demoted when it stops fitting
the system's offers need a budget: a system that proposes structure at every regularity it spots re-creates the interruption it was meant to avoid

situation.initiating: … an actor or a group works with information across many surfaces, channels, and moments, and needs to understand where things are, how they relate, and what can be done with them.
situation.resulting: Keep every channel the actor reaches the environment through—web, phone, email, notification, or agent reply—opening onto the same items under the same names with [cross-channel continuity](/patterns/cross-channel-continuity). Build [searching](/patterns/searching) on the structure and vocabulary the environment keeps, so queries find items under the names the actor meets everywhere else, and use [dynamic hyperlinks](/patterns/dynamic-hyperlinks) to connect related items across sections and surfaces from within the content itself. Govern access through [sharing](/patterns/sharing) so grants follow the environment's containers and the structure the actor learns is also the structure of access…

resulting.clause: the second commitment happened where the first one did, so the actor was interrupted without being relocated — one decision of friction rather than a change of place

an armed control is a state the interface has to manage: it reverts on its own after a moment, and it has to look different enough from resting that the actor can tell a loaded control from an idle one
confirming is not reversing — the actor consented before the act and has nothing to undo after it, so anything that might still need taking back needs its own route

situation.initiating: the exchange has reached a point where words are the wrong vehicle — the actor needs to pick from a set, confirm one specific thing, nudge a value, read a chart — and putting it in prose asks them to do the rendering in their head

resulting.clause: the message is a thing to act on rather than words to read, so dialogue and application share one surface and the actor never leaves the conversation to do the work
interface rendered into a stream inherits the stream's properties: it scrolls away, it persists in the history, and a control the actor left untouched several turns ago is still sitting there live
what the actor did inline has to read afterwards as a decision rather than as a widget left in a state — the transcript is now a record of actions as well as words

situation.initiating: an activity is under way and the agent is missing something it can't infer — a required value, a constraint, a choice between candidates it can't rank — so the work stops until the actor supplies it

resulting.clause: the missing value is captured and confirmed, and the activity resumes at the step that needed it

the actor has been asked directly, which sets the expectation that the agent only asks for what it genuinely lacks; anything it could have inferred or defaulted now reads as busywork when it asks again

situation.initiating: the exchange is open and the actor has a question the agent can answer as asked — nothing to disambiguate first, no multi-step work behind it

resulting.clause: the question is answered and the pair is complete; the actor is between activities rather than inside one, free to follow up, check the source, or start something else
a direct answer carries no working, so for anything non-trivial the actor is taking the agent's word for it unless evidence came with the answer

situation.initiating: … in [delegating a task](/sequences/delegating-a-task), the actor has asked for something with a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) and received [generated content](/patterns/generated-content)—a draft, a reply, or a passage in a document—that is close, with a flaw they can name. Rather than drawing again with [regeneration](/patterns/regeneration), they want to steer the draft already in front of them.
situation.resulting: Scope revisions to a [selection](/patterns/selection) so an instruction does not disturb passages the actor has already settled, and offer quick revision presets as [suggestions](/patterns/suggestion) beside an open instruction field. Keep the replaced version one step back through [undo](/patterns/undo), and where a revision rewrites several places at once, present it through [change review](/patterns/change-review) against the last accepted version so the actor can accept or reject changes in parts. Where revision runs through a conversation, pair it with a [steering surface](/patterns/steering-surface) that holds the work still beside the instructions so the actor does not carry each revised version back by hand. Where a change is a single word, figure, or name the actor already has in mind, hand off to [editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place); where the actor repeats the same correction across outputs, promote it to [standing instructions](/patterns/standing-instructions). Where others need to know that machine revision shaped a passage, mark it with [provenance marking](/patterns/provenance-marking)…

situation.initiating: an entity must appear somewhere — inside running text, among its peers, on its own — and the moment fixes how much of it the actor needs: bare recognition, quick comparison, or a full working surface

resulting.clause: the entity renders at the level of detail its moment needs and remains recognisable as the same entity at every level
moving between levels is a designed transition, not a page reload — context survives the shift in depth

situation.initiating: the actor already knows what they want and has done it often enough for it to be motor memory; the interface path they would otherwise take is now the slowest part of the operation

resulting.clause: intent goes straight to execution without traversing the interface — for the actors who have the vocabulary
the vocabulary is invisible by construction, so knowing that shortcuts exist and using them stay separate events, and the gap between them has to be closed somewhere the actor is already looking
the set is a fixed budget: every binding added dilutes what can be internalised, and the platform conventions are already spent

situation.initiating: … the artifact holds a wide toolset serving both basic and specialised workflows, and [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) has to bring newcomers into working use of it. This pattern instantiates [progressive disclosure](/patterns/progressive-disclosure) across sessions and developing competence rather than within a single view.
situation.resulting: For capabilities held back from the active layer, omit them from the surface as [unavailable actions](/patterns/unavailable-actions) when keeping the view uncluttered matters most, or show them in a [disabled state](/patterns/state-disabled) with a path to unlock them when the actor needs to see what higher layers hold. Keep the layer switch visible and store the choice in [settings](/patterns/settings) as a lasting preference so stepping up stays under the actor's control, and use [feature discovery](/patterns/feature-discovery) to offer the switch when the actor's work reaches a hidden capability. Treat outgrowing the reduced layers as a step toward [mastery](/patterns/mastery), keeping control positions stable as fuller layers open…

situation.initiating: the content is densely cross-referenced and every link is a fork in the actor's attention; finding out whether a link was worth following costs the reading position, so the actor either clicks indiscriminately or stops clicking

resulting.clause: the actor can sample a destination without leaving their place, so triage happens at the link rather than after the navigation — follow it, skip it, or note it for later

the page now owes the actor a ladder of commitment rather than one click: peek, open alongside, open fully — and each rung has to be reachable by keyboard as well as by hover, since hover is the one channel touch doesn't have

situation.initiating: generation takes seconds to minutes, and a silent wait reads as failure; the actor can neither judge nor act on the answer until something of it shows

resulting.clause: the output is legible as it forms, so the actor can skim ahead of the machine, judge early — and stop early, which is what makes interruption meaningful mid-generation
reading begins before the whole exists: early text anchors the actor's take even when later text qualifies or contradicts it
