the arrival rhythm is now part of the interface — pace, pauses, and re-layout as content lands are designed properties, not transport details
once the stream completes, a produced artefact sits on the surface — the move shifts from holding the rendering stable to negotiating what arrived

situation.initiating: … the artifact is placed among the [tools the actor already uses](/patterns/tool-ecology), and the work they make in it may need to outlast the artifact, the provider or the actor's subscription. Where the work lives is decided before any feature is built on it.
situation.resulting: Where the actor wants the same work on their other devices without creating an account, carry the files via [sync through own storage](/patterns/sync-through-own-storage), and keep accounts optional with [identity at the point of need](/patterns/identity-at-the-point-of-need). Pair the storage format with [import and export](/patterns/import-and-export) so the actor can move work to other programs without silent loss, and where offline copies can diverge across devices, settle collisions on return with [reconciliation](/patterns/reconciliation)…

situation.initiating: the actor is past learning the tool and is in it daily; the scaffolding that got them started is now in the way, and what caps them is the interface rather than their understanding of the work

resulting.clause: there are optional routes to expertise that nobody has to take, so the perpetual intermediates stay productive while the few who want depth can find it
the expert reshapes the tool around their own way of working, which means the tool has to have parts that move
a surface tuned for mastery is denser than a beginner can read, so one system has to serve both without splitting into two
actors mostly pick up the optional routes from someone working beside them who already uses them, which the artifact can make visible but cannot arrange

situation.initiating: … the actor works with an [agent](/patterns/agent) across multiple [sessions](/patterns/session), carrying background facts, preferences, and recurring project context that go beyond explicit rules in [standing instructions](/patterns/standing-instructions). Memory helps complete multi-session work when the system retains details about the actor from ongoing exchanges.
situation.resulting: Carry stored facts and preferences into later runs to tailor [generated content](/patterns/generated-content). Whenever the system saves or updates a detail during an exchange, show [transient feedback](/patterns/transient-feedback) in place and attach a [citation](/patterns/citation) back to the conversation turn it came from. Expose the full store as a reviewable list in [settings](/patterns/settings) with [deletion](/patterns/deletion) for individual facts or topics, kept separate from past transcripts in the [activity log](/patterns/activity-log) so removing a memory does not quietly re-infer it. Let the actor set standing exclusions over topics that must never be stored with [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition), scope separate stores per [workspace](/patterns/workspace) where projects or roles differ, and offer an [ephemeral session](/patterns/ephemeral-session) when an exchange should stay outside memory and history altogether…

situation.initiating: … an agent is partway through a multi-step run under [delegation](/patterns/delegation), and its [work trail](/patterns/work-trail) or [working plan](/patterns/working-plan) shows a wrong assumption, a missing constraint, or a branch heading the wrong way. The work already done is worth keeping rather than cancelling with [abort](/patterns/abort).
situation.resulting: Mark the intervention point in the [work trail](/patterns/work-trail) so the actor can tell which steps came before and after the change. Where the actor wants to compare the corrected direction against the original path rather than replace it, offer [branching](/patterns/branching) from the disputed step. Where the run has already finished, use [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) instead, and where the agent cannot recover even with guidance, transfer the work back through a [handoff](/patterns/handoff)…

situation.initiating: the work has been partitioned into contexts, and this one holds heterogeneous sections with subsections behind them — enough pages that a flat surface cannot hold them and a global menu cannot name them, and a categorisation the actor can be expected to learn

resulting.clause: content sits at addresses the actor can learn and re-find, and the trail from the root to here is available as orientation without spending extra chrome on it
the hierarchy is now a standing guess about how the actor categorises, and it will be wrong for some content and some actors; a thing that belongs in two places has to be filed in one
lateral movement costs a trip back up: two sections that turn out to be related have no path between them that the structure recognises

situation.initiating: the actor is at a transition point in a workflow the system can read — it knows what they just finished and holds enough signal to name a plausible next step — and what's worth proposing is a whole action rather than a value, so nothing further down the completion spectrum reaches it

resulting.clause: the system proposes actions rather than values, so accepting one commits the actor to something whose consequences they didn't work out themselves; what guards the accept has to be proportional to what the action does
where the stakes are high, the recommendation being easy to accept is the problem rather than the feature — the accept needs a beat of deliberate thought built into it
recommendations now arrive uninvited, at moments the system picked; a pile of them nobody resolved teaches the actor to stop reading the channel at all

situation.initiating: a system event whose existence the actor needs to know about, alongside an existing flow that has its own demands on attention

resulting.clause: a delivery surface tuned to the event's urgency and the actor's availability

every notification spends attention the actor did not offer; when the spend outruns what the notifications are worth to them, they turn the channel off, and it then carries nothing, the urgent events included
a kind of event the actor keeps muting or dismissing unread was graded too high, and the muting is the evidence to regrade it on

situation.initiating: … an actor arrives at an artifact for the first time, through [immediate use](/patterns/immediate-use) or [account access](/patterns/account-access), and has no working model yet of what it holds, what their actions will do, or what it will do on its own. This is the start of the actor's [learning](/sequences/learning).
situation.resulting: Begin on the [empty state](/patterns/state-empty) of the surface the actor will work on, so the first view shows what belongs there and how to create it, and use [good defaults](/patterns/good-defaults) to settle decisions that do not change the first result. Give the actor a [template](/patterns/template) when they need a starting shape to fill, or a [starter example](/patterns/starter-example) when they need a finished item to inspect, modify, and clear. Use a [wizard](/patterns/wizard) only where early setup decisions depend on one another. Where the artifact has more capabilities than a newcomer can take in at once, hold advanced functions back in a [layered interface](/patterns/layered-interface), surface individual capabilities at the moment they become relevant through [feature discovery](/patterns/feature-discovery), and lay out the route across sittings with [charted progress](/patterns/charted-progress). Defer access grants until the actor triggers the feature that needs them, as [permissions](/patterns/permissions) prescribes. Where an [agent](/patterns/agent) will act on the actor's behalf, introduce what it can and cannot do during the first run and state its [capability and scope](/patterns/capability-and-scope) before the first turn. When the newcomer is entering a shared workspace that already holds other people's work, hand off orientation to what others built in it to [working on the same thing](/sequences/working-on-the-same-thing#joining). Leave unanticipated questions to [help](/patterns/help), which stays available after the first run ends, and let [mastery](/patterns/mastery) clear the first-run scaffolding away once the actor is working fluently…

situation.initiating: the actor has stated a goal rather than a step — complex enough that the agent can't act on it as given, with constraints missing and several moves between the request and the outcome

resulting.clause: the request is framed rather than merely received: goal, constraints, assumptions and sources are explicit, and what's still missing shows up as named gaps instead of general vagueness
a plan exists and the agent is about to act on the actor's behalf; where a step can't be taken back, the actor's explicit go-ahead has to come before it, not after

situation.initiating: … the artifact sits within the [tools the actor already works with](/patterns/tool-ecology), and the actor brings an AI agent of their own—an assistant that works across several of those tools—to read and act on the work in it. That agent answers to the actor rather than the artifact's maker, and arrives whether or not the artifact was designed for it.
situation.resulting: Let the actor issue and revoke the agent's grant through [sharing](/patterns/sharing), listing the agent beside the people who have access. Scope what it may do without asking through [bounded autonomy](/patterns/bounded-autonomy), and hold acts that need confirmation at an [approval gate](/patterns/approval-gate). Sign its contributions under its own name with [attribution](/patterns/attribution), and record its acts in the [activity log](/patterns/activity-log)…

situation.initiating: the decision has failure modes somebody can name in advance, and the actor accepting output isn't failing to think so much as failing to think about the right things; a delay would buy them time without telling them where to spend it

resulting.clause: the review is structured rather than gestalt — the actor has engaged with each named consideration before the accept became available to them
a required checklist creates compliance pressure, so each item either points somewhere the actor wouldn't have looked or it becomes a box to clear
the enumerated failure modes are now a standing artefact with an owner: the domain's failure modes move, and a checklist that doesn't move with them certifies the wrong things

situation.initiating: a collection framing exists and the actor works item by item — scanning many candidates, verifying one — but no single view is both compact enough to scan and rich enough to verify

resulting.clause: two linked views cover one collection — one compressed, one in full — and the actor moves between them without losing their place
the overview's attribute subset fixes what the actor can compare, sort, and filter by — a ceiling only malleability lifts

situation.initiating: the work has been partitioned into contexts, and this one holds a single continuous space — a map, a canvas, a timeline — where what the actor wants to reach is a place in it rather than a page; there is no sequence to walk and no collection to browse, so movement is viewport control

resulting.clause: everything keeps its place in one coordinate system, so nothing breaks the spatial sense — and orientation becomes the actor's problem: at any zoom the view carries no evidence of where it sits in the whole, which is what a second, wider viewport kept in step is for
a continuous space has no addresses of its own; position and scale have to be made nameable before anything in it can be linked to, bookmarked, or returned to
what's on screen is a fraction of what exists, so the space has to decide what to load and what detail to draw at each scale — and those are visible to the actor as waiting, not as engineering

situation.initiating: … [account access](/patterns/account-access) is in place on a [form](/patterns/form), and where [passwordless access](/patterns/passwordless-access) or [federated identity](/patterns/federated-identity) is not available or not chosen, the artifact asks for a password that depends on nothing outside itself. The actor is creating that secret or entering it from memory, a note, or a password manager.
situation.resulting: Surface requirements and rejections at the field—and before submission where possible—through [validation](/patterns/validation). Because a forgotten password is routine rather than exceptional, keep [account recovery](/patterns/account-recovery) in reach from the sign-in step…

situation.initiating: … [account access](/patterns/account-access) is in place for registration and sign-in, and the actor already controls an email address or phone rather than relying on a standalone [password](/patterns/password).
situation.resulting: Where actors prefer to sign in through an external provider rather than wait for a message or code, offer [federated identity](/patterns/federated-identity) instead, and where an actor lacks reliable access to an inbox or phone, keep a [password](/patterns/password) alongside it…

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes), [automatic saving](/patterns/automatic-saving) will not work because the change only makes sense as a unit—a [form](/patterns/form) whose fields depend on each other, a [settings](/patterns/settings) panel, a batch of deletions, or a storage constraint that accepts whole records only. Applying half the edit would leave the artifact in an incoherent state, or the actor needs a genuine way to abandon the attempt.
situation.resulting: Show the uncommitted state clearly through [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback), and pair with [resuming](/patterns/resuming) where pending edits need to survive an interruption. Where the pending set is large or the commitment costly, pass it through [review before submitting](/patterns/review-before-submitting) before applying it. Where pending edits include removals, stage them as a batch alongside [deletion](/patterns/deletion) so one action confirms or cancels the lot. Where two actors hold overlapping pending edits on the same artifact, settle the clash at commit time with [reconciliation](/patterns/reconciliation)…

situation.initiating: … to carry out a task, the artifact needs access to something the actor controls outside it—a camera or location sensor, local files, contacts, or an external account such as a calendar or mailbox—either for a feature the actor just triggered or for an [agent](/patterns/agent) working under [delegation](/patterns/delegation).
situation.resulting: Put the list of active grants in [settings](/patterns/settings) so the actor can inspect and revoke them later; withdraw standing grants when the work ends, and let unused grants lapse after a set time. Once an external source is connected, let the actor attach items from it as [reference material](/patterns/reference-material). Where an agent uses the connection, pair these grants with [bounded autonomy](/patterns/bounded-autonomy) to settle what the agent may do there without asking…

situation.initiating: … the actor has made an [open request](/patterns/open-request) of an agent for multi-step work with real consequences, and [showing the reading](/patterns/showing-the-reading) has settled what the request means. The work may run in reply or be handed over in [delegation](/patterns/delegation).
situation.resulting: Pair the plan with [cost transparency](/patterns/cost-transparency) to state expected spend, and place an [approval gate](/patterns/approval-gate) in front of the whole run so work waits until the actor starts it. Carry the approved steps straight into the [working plan](/patterns/working-plan) as the run proceeds, and expose the actions and reasoning behind each step through a [work trail](/patterns/work-trail). Gate which requests warrant a preview using [action consequences](/patterns/action-consequences) so routine low-stakes work does not turn plan review into a ritual…

situation.initiating: several people work on the same thing behind separate screens; each can scroll to a different part, so the workspace shows everyone everything except each other, and what a shared desk answered in a glance — who is here, where, doing what — now costs an interruption to ask

resulting.clause: who is present, where they are working, and what they are doing reads in passing, at grades matched to the tempo — an avatar stack, a named cursor and selection, an action signal, an after-the-fact trail — and people self-partition around what they can see, so most collisions never happen
the marks must be by-products of working, never authored reports: an authored report costs its provider and pays someone else, so it goes unfed
visibility is also being watched: past some point the marks change what people dare explore, and the freedom to make mistakes moves to tools that cannot see

situation.initiating: … the actor is composing text inside a [form](/patterns/form), a reply when [commenting](/patterns/commenting), a message in a [conversation](/patterns/conversation), or a document in a [block-based editor](/patterns/block-based-editor), and needs to mark hierarchy and emphasis directly in the flow of writing, much as [editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place) keeps edits on the surface itself.
situation.resulting: Offer the role set as a [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) sized to the writing surface, and surface it directly at the caret through a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) or [keyboard shortcuts](/patterns/keyboard-shortcuts). Because each role marks meaning rather than appearance, let the actor promote or change roles over time through [incremental formalisation](/patterns/incremental-formalisation) without restyling the text…

situation.initiating: a purpose recurs so predictably that the domain can state, by consensus and in advance, what counts as a problem — yet on every visit the actor still triages a general view by inference, re-deriving the same judgements the rules could carry

resulting.clause: what needs attention arrives as a rule-backed checklist — index, navigation, status display and audit trail at once — and every flag can say why it fired

the rule set is a standing maintenance duty — to its reader a false positive is any flag they did not want to see, so flags need a feedback channel and a noise budget, or the curve is alarm fatigue, then suppression: the checklist still renders after trust has left it
whatever the rules don't encode sails past; the general exploratory view remains the place to notice it

situation.initiating: the surface has more to say than the actor needs right now, and cutting the depth isn't available — the extra factors, controls and evidence are legitimate content that some actors genuinely need; showing all of it up front is what makes the common path hard to find

resulting.clause: the first view carries the common path and the depth stays reachable, so what detail costs the actor is proportional to their need for it

every deferred layer is a bet that this actor won't need it; a layer with no hint that it exists doesn't just cost a click when the bet is wrong — it leaves the actor with a wrong picture of what the system can do
what shows by default now carries the weight of a recommendation, because the actors who never expand read the first level as the whole answer

situation.initiating: … the actor has reached the point of framing a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) in [delegating a task](/sequences/delegating-a-task) for a recurring or high-constraint task whose relevant parameters can be anticipated in advance. Prompt scaffolding helps complete the prompt—and acts as a generative [template](/patterns/template)—where those parameters are known up front; where the intent is exploratory and the questions cannot be anticipated, an [open request](/patterns/open-request) drawn out through conversation serves better.
situation.resulting: Break each parameter into a separate control, using [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) where the value comes from a fixed set of options, criteria, or schemas. Check the request before it runs with [validation](/patterns/validation) to warn about missing parameters or underspecified instructions at the field that needs attention. Where starter values help illustrate the slots, offer them through [suggestion](/patterns/suggestion), keeping them light so they do not anchor the actor or narrow output diversity. When a scaffold requires several interdependent configuration steps, paginate the flow with a [wizard](/patterns/wizard). When a working scaffold configuration recurs across tasks, save it as a [template](/patterns/template) with fillable slots, and keep an open-text escape or path to an [open request](/patterns/open-request) when the task outgrows the fixed slots…

situation.initiating: … the actor is working in a [conversation](/patterns/conversation), inside a bounded [session](/patterns/session), with an [agent](/patterns/agent) in [delegating a task](/sequences/delegating-a-task), or anywhere in an artifact [addressable in words](/patterns/addressable-in-words). A prompt helps complete these larger patterns when the actor's intent has no dedicated control or command name to reach it by; where it does, a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) reaches it faster and more predictably.
situation.resulting: Where a blank input leaves the actor unsure what the system can do, host starter [suggestions](/patterns/suggestion) on the prompt surface to seed an example request. Let the actor attach or @-mention [reference material](/patterns/reference-material) inside the prompt, and read what they already have open or selected through [view as context](/patterns/view-as-context) so they do not have to name what is in front of them. Where the task is repetitive and high-constraint and open prose keeps leaving required parameters out, structure the input with [prompt scaffolding](/patterns/prompt-scaffolding); where the request is complex and missing constraints would be costly to guess wrong, treat it as an [open request](/patterns/open-request) and let [agent inquiry](/patterns/inquiry-agent) ask back for what is missing. Feed the submitted prompt and its bound context into [generated content](/patterns/generated-content), then follow the initial output with [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) to steer what came back or [regeneration](/patterns/regeneration) to draw another attempt. When a working prompt recurs across items, let the actor save it as a [template](/patterns/template); when the same instruction has to be repeated in every session, promote it to [standing instructions](/patterns/standing-instructions) so it holds on every run…

situation.initiating: … the system has produced [generated content](/patterns/generated-content) that will sit alongside human writing, or work is leaving the surface that made it through [import and export](/patterns/import-and-export). The same situation arises when a passage has been rewritten through [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) or adapted through a [text lens](/patterns/text-lens). Provenance marking helps complete these patterns when later readers need to tell machine output from human wording.
situation.resulting: Where marked output makes factual claims, pair the origin mark with [citation](/patterns/citation) so the actor can see both that the system wrote a claim and which source passage backs it. Because a visible disclosure mark can reassure on sight without prompting closer reading, add [cognitive forcing functions](/patterns/cognitive-forcing-functions) at acceptance where the stakes of acting on wrong output are high. In shared workspaces, pair provenance marking with [attribution](/patterns/attribution) to record which person, delegated agent, or rule made each edit or comment across the work…

situation.initiating: the data is already well presented — a collection framing renders it legibly, nothing is hidden — yet the actor's recurring question (is anything wrong? what is happening? what changed?) still takes inference to answer, and different moments bring the question with radically different attention budgets

resulting.clause: each recurring purpose has a view designed for its own question and attention budget, instead of one general view compromising across all of them
every purpose-keyed view is a curation decision someone must maintain — whatever it omits, the actor must know to ask for

the general exploratory view stays reachable from every purpose-keyed one — curation prunes it, never replaces it, because the purposes only anticipate the questions they encode and cases outside them need somewhere to be noticed

situation.initiating: the work has been partitioned into contexts, and this one is an ordered sequence — a course, a gallery, a series — whose order is worth offering but whose items do not depend on each other, so nothing is lost by letting the actor enter anywhere

resulting.clause: the sequence is legible as a whole and enterable at any point, so an actor who wants the order gets it and an actor who wants item nine doesn't have to earn it through the first eight
the hub has to state the shape of the sequence — how long it is, where this item sits in it — or the offer of sequential reading is one the actor can't judge
progress is now something the actor accumulates and expects to be remembered; a sequence that forgets where they stopped is one they restart

situation.initiating: … the actor needs something the artifact cannot do on its own: access to a document someone else controls, a permission only an admin can grant, an account they cannot get back into after [account recovery](/patterns/account-recovery) has failed, a review of a decision made about them, a charge they dispute. [Help](/patterns/help) has nothing more to tell them, because the fix needs access, authority, judgement or knowledge that some person holds: the owner of the item, a workspace admin, a contact the actor named in advance, a moderator, or the provider's support.
situation.resulting: Where an agent was already working on the task or triaging the conversation before passing it on, use [handoff](/patterns/handoff) to package the progress so far and govern the transfer of responsibility and any return to the agent…

situation.initiating: … [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking) gives items and views stable addresses that restore them, and [bookmarking](/patterns/bookmarking) covers what the actor explicitly chose to keep. Here the actor wants to return to something from earlier in the session or the day—a file from this morning, yesterday's conversation, or a search from before lunch—that they did not save at the time.
situation.resulting: Surface the list at navigation starting points such as a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu) before a query is typed or the [empty state](/patterns/state-empty) of a workspace. Feed recent entries into [autocomplete](/patterns/autocomplete) so the actor's own recent items rank above system guesses. Where an [activity log](/patterns/activity-log) already exists, project recents from it by deduplicating and trimming rather than maintaining a second store. On shared screens or for sensitive tasks, pair recents with [ephemeral session](/patterns/ephemeral-session) so off-the-record work never enters the list…

situation.initiating: … in [working on the same thing](/sequences/working-on-the-same-thing), two lines of work parted under [draft and publish](/patterns/draft-and-publish)—as a branch, a separate draft, or a stretch offline—and now one returns alongside [change review](/patterns/change-review). Both sides have edited the same part of the work.
situation.resulting: Show the colliding versions with [comparing](/patterns/comparing)'s version case so the actor picks on the difference rather than scanning two full copies. Treat the unpicked version as a removal and give it [undo](/patterns/undo) as recovery. Where the work keeps a [version history](/patterns/version-history), retain the unpicked version in it, and route restoring an older version over a colleague's later edits back through reconciliation rather than overwriting silently…

situation.initiating: the request needs grounding the system does not have and cannot read from where the actor is — this document, that image, the actual dataset — and without it the system answers from generalities while sounding specific

resulting.clause: the output is anchored in named material, and can point back to it — the attachment that went in is what a citation can later point out
the attached material scopes the answer, so wrong, stale, or partial material scopes it wrong with the same confidence
supplying context grows into its own task: what began as attaching a file becomes curating a corpus the system works from

situation.initiating: … in [delegating a task](/sequences/delegating-a-task), the actor has asked for something with a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) and received [generated content](/patterns/generated-content) that misses the mark, while the intent behind the request still holds. They have no specific change to describe—where they can name what is off, [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) steers the output they have, and where they know the exact fix, [editing in place](/patterns/editing-in-place) applies it directly.
situation.resulting: Where most of the output already works, scope the redraw to a [selection](/patterns/selection) so the settled surroundings stay untouched. Keep the replaced result one step back through [undo](/patterns/undo) or version stepping on the turn. Where the actor returns to an earlier turn in a thread to try a different direction, fork the exchange with [branching](/patterns/branching) so the subsequent turns stay intact. When the actor draws several candidates at once, align them through [comparing](/patterns/comparing) so differences can be read directly rather than held in memory. Where a full run is slow or costly, pair regeneration with [draft and publish](/patterns/draft-and-publish) to redraw cheaply in a draft state before committing to the final result…

situation.initiating: … the actor returns to an artifact they adjusted during normal use—configuring a [data view](/patterns/data-view), selecting a tab, resizing a panel, scrolling partway through a document, or picking an export format—without visiting [settings](/patterns/settings). [Deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking) covers views that need a shareable URL; here the actor is simply coming back to their own working arrangement.
situation.resulting: Keep active criteria visible on the surface through [filtering](/patterns/filtering) so a restored filter never looks like missing data. Feed the actor's last-chosen option values into [good defaults](/patterns/good-defaults) as personal starting values for the next session. Where the actor also needs to jump back to other items they opened lately, pair this with [recents](/patterns/recents), and where work on a shared device should leave no trace, offer [ephemeral session](/patterns/ephemeral-session)…

situation.initiating: … the actor is partway through a task in a [wizard](/patterns/wizard) or a long form that will not finish in one sitting—they need information they do not have to hand, more time than they have now, or a quieter place to finish. They leave the task and return hours or weeks later.
situation.resulting: Confirm with [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) that the work is kept at the moment the actor leaves and again when it is restored on return. Where the return shows a full summary of entries after a long gap, share the view with [review before submitting](/patterns/review-before-submitting) so each entry links directly to where it can be edited. Where an account is the way back across devices, introduce it through [identity at the point of need](/patterns/identity-at-the-point-of-need) after the actor has already entered work rather than before they start…

situation.initiating: the actor has entered answers over several steps or down a long form, and the next action commits them: an order is placed, an application sent, an account or resource created. Most of what they entered is out of view, and some of it cannot be changed once committed

… [division of responsibility](/patterns/division-of-responsibility) has settled which parts of the work each party answers for. Inside one part of a [workspace](/patterns/workspace), people still take part in different ways: some run it, some contribute, some review and some only read.
situation.resulting: Offer these roles as the access levels in [sharing](/patterns/sharing) when letting people in. When an actor meets an action their role does not allow, use [explanation](/patterns/explanation) to name the role required—letting them ask for it from there—and use [unavailable actions](/patterns/unavailable-actions) to hide only the actions that are not theirs to ask for. Give an [outside agent](/patterns/outside-agent) a role in the same way, and limit what it may do there without asking through [bounded autonomy](/patterns/bounded-autonomy)…

situation.initiating: the actor wants the system to pick out cases by criteria of their own, either to narrow what is shown now or to stand as a rule the system acts on while they are away; the criteria have to be exact enough for the system to apply and clear enough for the actor to check

resulting.clause: the condition is visible as a statement whose parts can be read, changed, added and removed, so the actor can inspect what the system matches instead of only noticing it
reading the statement does not tell the actor what it matches or does; a selecting rule shows its result on the collection at once, an acting rule shows nothing until it fires
the words on offer are the system's, not the actor's, so a wish the parts cannot express gets approximated, and the approximation is what runs
when the rule acts, it runs alongside the rules already in place and together they decide the outcome; rules pile up, and past a certain size the actor can no longer keep the list in mind

situation.initiating: … in [composing views](/sequences/composing-views) a collection is already framed for browsing and [filtering](/patterns/filtering); in [structuring the space](/sequences/structuring-the-space) sections are arranged in a [multilevel tree](/patterns/multilevel-tree) or [hub and spoke](/patterns/hub-and-spoke) layout; and in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes) a [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) field holds more options than scan well inline. Searching helps complete the [information environment](/patterns/information-environment) built on the names, content, and [tags](/patterns/tag) of its [information architecture](/patterns/information-architecture), serving actors who know a word or phrase rather than where an item sits.
situation.resulting: Present the ranked results in a [data view](/patterns/data-view) and make each query state addressable through [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking). At the input, pair the query box with [recents](/patterns/recents) before typing begins and [autocomplete](/patterns/autocomplete) as the actor types to complete terms or jump straight to a known item. On the results, pair the ranked list with [suggestions](/patterns/suggestion) for query refinements, [filtering](/patterns/filtering) over facets to narrow the set in place, and [navigation](/patterns/navigation-overview) when the query falls short. Where the query targets the artifact's actions and destinations rather than its content, specialise into a [command menu](/patterns/command-menu)…

situation.initiating: content that divides into a small, stable set of named parts where which-mode-to-show is a property of context, not of the content

resulting.clause: a single container whose disclosure affordance (tabs vs. accordion) shifts with context without restructuring the content

situation.initiating: a moment where the actor must designate members of an exposed set of options

resulting.clause: a designation — narrowed by scanning or typing — whose fate (committed value, staked target, spliced text) is set by the surrounding flow

situation.initiating: the space is too large to take in at once and plain magnification fails in both directions — pulling back shrinks everything to unreadable specks, moving in loses the shape of the whole; the items do have small forms that stay recognisable, which is what makes swapping representation available instead of resizing

resulting.clause: every distance shows one uniform level of representation, so the population reads consistently at each scale and the actor learns what a given zoom level means

representations don't interpolate — a dot, a title and a paragraph are different artefacts — so thresholds are unavoidable, and where they sit and how the crossing is presented become the design rather than a detail of it
a richer rung has to fit the box its coarser neighbour occupied, or the arrangement the zoom was protecting comes apart on the way out

situation.initiating: an activity has just delivered what the actor asked for, and the exchange is at the third position: the agent can see the sequence finished but not that it landed, and only the actor's receipt tells the difference

resulting.clause: the sequence is closed from the actor's side and the encounter is between activities; if this was the last thing they came for, the encounter itself is ready to be ended rather than left open
an acknowledged completion is the natural place to offer a next move and the easiest place to over-prompt — the actor may simply be finished

the turns, attached context, and intermediate results of the task accumulate inside one bounded thread, so each new [prompt](/patterns/prompt) only has to state what is new rather than re-supplying what was already said and done

earlier turns, rejected attempts, and stale assumptions stay in scope as the session grows and continue to steer later outputs, so starting a fresh session becomes a deliberate reset when the task changes

because the session has a title and a place in a history list, the actor can leave the exchange and return to it later, while anything that needs to outlive the thread has to be lifted out through [extraction](/patterns/extraction) or promoted to [memory](/patterns/memory) or [standing instructions](/patterns/standing-instructions)

situation.initiating: the defaults serve most actors and this one isn't among them on some axis they care about enough to go looking; the difference is a preference rather than a pattern, so no amount of watching their behaviour would have inferred it

resulting.clause: the actor's overrides are recorded and the system holds to them, so an adaptation made once outlasts the session that made it
the surface accumulates: every option added is one more thing to look past, and the ones nobody ever changes still cost the actors hunting for the ones they do

a preference set once and honoured indefinitely stops being visible to the actor who set it, so behaviour that follows from it reads later as a fault rather than as their own earlier decision — the setting has to be named where the behaviour shows
in shared configuration, one actor's change alters what others see without their doing anything — something has to carry the change across to them

situation.initiating: … a [workspace](/patterns/workspace) holds a person's private work or the shared work of a team or organisation, and new items start with the access of the place they are made in. Where several parties take part in the work, [division of responsibility](/patterns/division-of-responsibility) draws the lines between the parts each party answers for and settles who may let others in. Soon someone outside a part, or outside the workspace altogether, needs to see, review or edit a folder or a single item without being given the rest.
situation.resulting: Assign each invited person or group one of the space's [roles](/patterns/roles), and let an [outside agent](/patterns/outside-agent) in or remove it through the same list without exceeding its bringer's access. Pair access links with [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking) so a link either opens only for people who already hold access or carries a role of its own for recipients without an account. Once several people open the same live work together, add [presence](/patterns/presence) to show who else is there and [commenting](/patterns/commenting) for roles that review or discuss. Where rough work should stay private until ready, separate the working copy with [draft and publish](/patterns/draft-and-publish)—or give each party its own part with its own access when they need different issued sets…

situation.initiating: … the actor has stated a request in an artifact [addressable in words](/patterns/addressable-in-words), through a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) or a turn in a [conversation](/patterns/conversation), and the words leave open what the request refers to or what it should do.
situation.resulting: Where several readings are plausible, show them side by side so the actor can pick one; where too much is missing to form a reading at all, hand off to [agent inquiry](/patterns/inquiry-agent) instead. Where the request maps onto structured criteria, render the reading as editable [filtering](/patterns/filtering) controls so individual terms can be adjusted in place. Once the reading is settled for multi-step work, follow it with a [plan preview](/patterns/plan-preview) to show what the artifact will do about it, and provide [agent repair](/patterns/agent-repair) for when a reading still turns out wrong…

situation.initiating: the collection has already been narrowed to the right items but arrives in an order chosen once for everyone — an order that answers some question, just not the one this actor brought

resulting.clause: the actor holds the order, and their choice persists, so coming back to the page doesn't undo the arrangement they left it in
order is itself a claim about what matters: whatever the collection is sorted by becomes the thing read first, whether or not that was the intent

situation.initiating: … the actor works with an [agent](/patterns/agent) across repeated sessions, using a [prompt](/patterns/prompt) to steer a single run and [instructed revision](/patterns/instructed-revision) to correct a single output. Some corrections recur across sessions and belong to the work as a whole rather than to one turn.
situation.resulting: Keep the controls for [memory](/patterns/memory) separate from standing instructions so a fact the actor erased from system memory does not survive unnoticed as an instruction. As instructions accumulate and begin to conflict, offer a [trial run](/patterns/trial-run) so the actor can test what an edited instruction file actually produces before relying on it. Where a standing rule must execute deterministically rather than by interpretation, use [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition); where a preference fits a fixed axis, put it in [settings](/patterns/settings); where a procedure should run only when invoked, build a [workflow](/patterns/workflow); and where the goal is to limit what the agent may do on its own, enforce it as a grant through [bounded autonomy](/patterns/bounded-autonomy) rather than as prose…

situation.initiating: … during [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding), the actor arrives at an [empty state](/patterns/state-empty) on a surface—such as a board, a database, a timeline, or an analytics view—whose structure and value only become clear once it holds populated content. A [template](/patterns/template) gives the actor an empty frame to fill, but not a finished instance they can inspect and manipulate before creating their own.
situation.resulting: Pair the example with a [template](/patterns/template) so that once the actor has seen how a finished item is put together, they have a clean structure ready for their own work. Keep the sample content isolated from live metrics, notifications, and exports, and let the actor remove all of it in a single action as soon as their own work begins…

situation.initiating: the alternatives have been ruled out: the element can't be hidden without breaking spatial memory or concealing capability, and it can't stay interactive with an explanation of why it can't act yet — disabling is the move that remains when the element must stay visible and genuinely cannot respond

… a surface that normally holds a collection, document, or view has nothing to show—on first use before anything has been created, after a search or filter excludes every item, once a queue is cleared, or behind a permission boundary.
situation.resulting: On first use, host [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding) inside the empty state so the first-run flow lands on the surface the actor will actually work in. Where starting from nothing is slow, offer a [template](/patterns/template) that gives the actor a structure to fill, or host a [starter example](/patterns/starter-example) on the surface so they can inspect a finished item and clear it when ready. For filtered, searched, cleared, or restricted views, design a dedicated empty state for each condition rather than reusing the first-run blank slate…

situation.initiating: the actor acts on their work by instructing rather than by touching it — in language, in commands — and the instructions and the work compete for the same space: held in one stream, the work fragments across the acts that changed it and scrolls away between them

resulting.clause: the work holds still on a surface of its own while the acts on it accumulate on another, so the current state is read in one place and the history of how it got there in the other

two surfaces now claim the truth: the instruction surface records what was asked and agreed, the work itself records what actually happened, and a change made directly on the work does not narrate itself back into the instructions

the two surfaces overlap on the work rather than rendering it twice, so only what both of them name can be coupled; the rest — talk with no counterpart in the work, changes made with no turn behind them — is a residue the design has to decide what to do with
the arrangement spends a permanent split of the screen, and the split has a direction: whichever surface is given the room is the one the design says the work happens on

situation.initiating: the work has been partitioned into contexts, and this one is an ordered sequence whose later steps depend on what earlier ones settle — a checkout, a setup — so letting the actor enter anywhere would hand them steps they cannot yet answer

resulting.clause: one decision is in front of the actor at a time and the order is the system's responsibility rather than theirs — which is the whole benefit, and the reason an actor who already knows where they need to be can't get there
the sequence is now a commitment the actor is partway into, so it owes them a way to leave and come back: what's been entered has to survive a stop
the steps are the system's model of the task, and where the actor's task doesn't decompose that way there is nowhere to put the difference

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes), a [form](/patterns/form) or a [wizard](/patterns/wizard) step needs a value with a strict, familiar syntax—such as a card number, licence key, or verification code—where [forgiving format](/patterns/forgiving-format) parsing would risk a costly misreading.
situation.resulting: Follow entry with [validation](/patterns/validation) at the field, since a value that matches the syntax can still fail semantic checks such as an expired card or an unknown code. Adapt the shape through [localization](/patterns/localization) wherever formats vary by region, and preserve single-field semantics so [autofill](/patterns/autofill) can supply stored records cleanly. Where the value must come from a fixed set rather than a formatted string, use [bounded choice](/patterns/bounded-choice) instead…

situation.initiating: the actor faces a blank or a wide choice the system has grounds to narrow — context, their history, or a model under which some continuations are far likelier than others — and starting from nothing is the real cost of the step

resulting.clause: the actor's option space now contains a concrete proposal, which is the help and also the anchor: shown before they have formed their own idea, it narrows what they go on to consider, and the alternatives they never reached aren't visible to them as a loss
accepting is one gesture and declining is a judgement, so the offer only stays an offer while dismissing it is cheaper than weighing it
a suggestion arriving without its confidence reads as an assertion; the actor needs to know how firm the ground under it is to weigh it against what they already think

situation.initiating: … the actor keeps their work in an artifact on their own device under [local-first ownership](/patterns/local-first-ownership), works on it alone, and wants it on every device they use, or kept safe off the device, through [identity at the point of need](/patterns/identity-at-the-point-of-need). They already have storage that follows them, such as iCloud, Dropbox or another service, and it is one of the [tools they already work with](/patterns/tool-ecology).
situation.resulting: Where edits on two devices can collide before the storage provider syncs them, settle the clash with [reconciliation](/patterns/reconciliation) rather than leaving an opaque conflicted copy beside the original. Surface sync state with [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) so the actor can tell when a device is still behind. Where another tool cannot read the synced files directly, pair the storage format with [import and export](/patterns/import-and-export)…

situation.initiating: the items belong to more than one category at once and a hierarchy would force the choice of one; the vocabulary that describes them is still moving too, so a taxonomy settled in advance would be wrong before it was finished

resulting.clause: items carry as many labels as apply, so the same item is reachable from several directions without being duplicated or re-filed
an applied label is a handle: whatever has been tagged becomes a facet to narrow by, which is where the value of tagging is actually collected
the labels are a shared vocabulary nobody controls — near-synonyms accumulate, and a label's meaning drifts with whoever is applying it

situation.initiating: the actor needs to produce something with a conventional shape they don't yet hold — a report, a plan, a prompt — and the atomic tools are all there; what's missing is the form, and a blank surface asks them to invent it before they can start

resulting.clause: the actor starts from a shape that already reflects competent work, and occupying it teaches the form in a way describing it wouldn't
the template is now a default the actor may not realise they can leave, so whatever it happens to prescribe gets treated as required
a set of templates is a curation with an owner: the conventions they encode drift, and the templates keep proposing last year's shape until somebody revisits them

situation.initiating: … the artifact holds [help](/patterns/help) documentation, articles, or records that serve readers with different background knowledge, or uses [semantic zoom](/patterns/semantic-zoom) and [focus and context](/patterns/focus-and-context) over prose. A text lens helps complete these larger patterns when a reader needs the same document at a different length, reading level, or language without altering the original.
situation.resulting: Treat each adapted view as [generated content](/patterns/generated-content) derived from the original so the actor can step back or redraw it without touching the source. Anchor claims in a shortened view to their source passages with [citation](/patterns/citation) so the summary leads back into the document rather than replacing it. Mark the adapted view with [provenance marking](/patterns/provenance-marking) wherever the actor needs to distinguish the author's wording from generated text…

situation.initiating: … an actor, or a group of actors, already works with many tools, accounts and agents, and the artifact being made will join that set rather than replace it.
situation.resulting: Decide where the work lives—on the provider's server or on the actor's device—under [local-first ownership](/patterns/local-first-ownership) before building features on top of it. Let work move out by reference through [deep linking](/patterns/deep-linking), and where a copy is needed, provide [import and export](/patterns/import-and-export) that states what the copy leaves behind. Keep a sign of origin on work that leaves the artifact with [provenance marking](/patterns/provenance-marking), and accept material brought in from other tools as [reference material](/patterns/reference-material). Let an agent the actor brings act on the artifact as an [outside agent](/patterns/outside-agent) under an explicit grant. Rely on what the actor already holds where it fits: sign them in through [federated identity](/patterns/federated-identity), support [autofill](/patterns/autofill) from the browser or password manager, and offer [sync through own storage](/patterns/sync-through-own-storage) where they already maintain their own storage…

situation.initiating: a recent action whose outcome the actor would benefit from confirming, without needing acknowledgement before continuing

resulting.clause: a brief peripheral message that auto-dismisses after a short window, optionally carrying a single trailing affordance such as undo

situation.initiating: … the actor has configured a bulk edit, a standing rule in [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition), a step inside a [workflow](/patterns/workflow), or an agent set to start by itself under [bounded autonomy](/patterns/bounded-autonomy). The setup is ready to activate, and the items it will act on are out of view or have not arrived yet.
situation.resulting: Attach an [explanation](/patterns/explanation) to each trial result showing which condition matched—and for filtering or selection rules, include the cases that narrowly missed—so the actor can spot a right outcome reached for the wrong reason. Where the trial previews edits to existing items, pass the batch into [change review](/patterns/change-review) so individual changes can be accepted or rejected before committing. Because a sample cannot cover every future input, pair live runs with [case correction](/patterns/case-correction) for unanticipated cases that misfire later…

situation.initiating: … the actor is configuring or correcting an [agent](/patterns/agent) under [delegation](/patterns/delegation)—or a tool such as a spreadsheet—where the desired tone, route, or handling of a case does not fit [standing instructions](/patterns/standing-instructions) in words or [rule composition](/patterns/rule-composition) in system terms. The actor can perform the task once or point to an instance done well.
situation.resulting: Store what was inferred in plain words inside [memory](/patterns/memory) so the actor can inspect and edit it alongside preferences picked up from ordinary use. Where the actor points to an existing sample, attach it as [reference material](/patterns/reference-material) paired with what about it to follow; where the actor records a multi-step procedure, turn it into an inspectable [workflow](/patterns/workflow) they can read and repair. Because a single demonstration fits many generalisations, follow it with a [trial run](/patterns/trial-run) over new cases before relying on the learned rule…

situation.initiating: an action exists in the surface's vocabulary but doesn't apply to what the actor is looking at, and the alternatives have been weighed: showing it inert puts a thing they can't use in front of them, and this isn't an action they need to know about here

resulting.clause: the surface carries only what applies, so nothing the actor can see is unusable
an action never shown is an action the actor may not know exists, which puts the full range of what's possible somewhere other than the current context or nowhere at all
hiding changes the layout, so the same surface has a different shape in different states — which spatial memory and assistive technology both read as things moving

situation.initiating: a recently committed action whose consequences the actor wants to retract

resulting.clause: a reverse path that returns the structure to its prior state

situation.initiating: the actor arrives with something already in mind and speaks first; the agent has no proposed topic to fall back on and has to recognise the opening and align to whatever was brought

resulting.clause: the actor's topic is on the table and the agent has aligned to it; the shape of what they brought decides the activity — a question answerable in one turn passes straight into user inquiry, a goal with steps behind it into an open request, and one stated too loosely to act on needs the agent to ask first
the actor has named a topic but nothing has been acted on yet, so an immediate change of mind costs nothing to honour

situation.initiating: the agent has said something that didn't land — an unfamiliar term, a step stated too fast, an assumption the actor doesn't share — and the activity can't move on until it does; the trouble is in the actor's comprehension, not in the agent's reading of the request

resulting.clause: the utterance has been re-delivered in another form — paraphrase, definition, worked example — and where none of those are enough the agent has to stop answering in single turns and take the floor properly
comprehension is restored with the activity mid-flight, so completion has to be able to resume from the same step — and still end in the receipt that closes the sequence

situation.initiating: … in [making changes](/sequences/making-changes) or the first encounter of [learning](/sequences/learning)—including first-time setup in [onboarding](/patterns/onboarding)—the actor faces an unfamiliar task whose early answers decide which questions exist later. situation.resulting: Throughout, let [status feedback](/patterns/status-feedback) say where the actor is, what failed, and at the end what the submission produced. Where the flow runs longer than one sitting, give it [resuming](/patterns/resuming), and ask before any exit that would discard what was entered.
